To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“Deep Learning-based methods are the most effective in detecting image-to-image translation fakes.

(1) GAN-generated fake images can be detected with high accuracy by both conventional and Deep Learning detectors; (2) Deep Learning-based detectors can still provide high accuracy even in the presence of JPEG compression; (3) JPEG compression reduces the detection accuracy of conventional methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection of fake images, and more specifically with the detection of GAN-generated images, in a real-world scenario, where the images are uploaded to a social network, compressed and shared.
the following aspects: (1) the detection of GAN-generated fake images over social networks, (2) the evaluation of the impact of compression on the detection performance.

the following contributions: 1) a large scale dataset of 36300 images, with ground truth annotations of the presence or not of image-to-image translation; 2) an analysis of the performance of conventional and deep learning based detectors, in the presence of image-to-image translations, and of compression; 3) a study of the performance of the best performing detector, in presence of compression and of the JPEG quantization table used.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the detection of GAN-generated fake images is possible, but the detection performance decreases when the images are compressed.
the use of GANs to generate fake images is a serious threat, but the detection of such fakes is still possible.

, while deep learning detectors are not able to provide an accurate detection in the presence of GAN-generated fakes, they still provide a better accuracy than conventional detectors in the presence of JPEG compression, which is routinely performed upon uploading images to social networks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GAN-generated images can be detected, but the detection accuracy is significantly lower than that of traditional fakes, and it is even lower for compressed images.
GAN-based fake image detectors can be trained to provide a high detection accuracy even when the input images are heavily compressed.
GAN-based image translation is a dangerous threat, but it can be mitigated by deep learning detectors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
deep learning detectors can be used to detect GAN-fake images, and that they can still work in presence of compression.
the use of GANs to generate fake images is still a challenge for detectors, especially when images are processed by a social network.

deep learning detectors can be used as a reliable tool for the detection of image-to-image translation attacks on compressed images, and thus for the detection of GAN-generated fake images over social networks.
